$comment: C10 · what a log's history costs in resident memory, before and after paging (I-10).
Produced by: cargo test --release -p schweep-soak --test c10_log_residency -- --nocapture
MACHINE-DEPENDENT: resident memory is an allocator and kernel figure, so no test recomputes
these rows. The gate asserts a SHARE rather than a value, so it means the same thing on any
The measurement is a difference, not a value: resident memory has a floor that has nothing to
do with the log, and quoting a value would be quoting the floor. So the gate opens a log over a
small history and over a ten-times-larger one and asks what the extra history cost.

before_c10.$comment: Not re-measured here — it is what C9's own gates measured of the design this replaces, and it is quoted so the after-figure has something to be against.
before_c10.design: Log kept every sealed batch resident (sealed: Vec<Vec<Batch>>) and read the whole segment with read_to_end at open

after_c10.design: Log holds an EpochSpan (16 bytes) per epoch; Log::epoch reads the records from the segment; the open scan and compaction both stream
after_c10.verdict: PASSED: ten times the history cost 1.53% of it in resident memory

dedup_index.why_it_exists: I-4 — a token forgotten is a batch that can be applied twice. Bounding it needs a retention policy, which is a decision and not an optimisation.
dedup_index.status: measured and reported by Log::dedup_len; NOT bounded

span_index.status: bounded by the epoch count, reported by Log::index_bytes

correctness.$comment: Performance work may not move a result byte (I-1). What was re-run against the paged log:
correctness.span_index_vs_full_scan: agrees epoch for epoch over 241 epochs
